policy.name: Madhya Pradesh MSME Development Policy, 2025 (Department of MSME, GoMP)
policy.order_no: Notification No. F 0057/2025/1/65 (as cited by TeamLease RegTech; not seen in official text)
policy.source_url: https://teamleaseregtech.com/updates/article/39993/madhya-pradesh-msme-development-policy-2025/ (secondary listing; the attached notification PDF has been removed; no official mp.gov.in copy reachable)

zone_lookup: Not confirmed. The companion MP Investment Promotion Scheme 2025 for LARGE units (NSWS copy, Annexure A 'List of Priority Blocks', doc p.53) uses Priority Blocks for a geographical multiple. Whether and how the MSME Policy 2025 uses priority blocks for MSMEs could not be confirmed from the official text.

schemes.name: Industrial Development Subsidy (units with P&M investment up to Rs 10 crore)
schemes.clause: MSME Development Policy 2025, section 7.1.1(i)-(iv) (per ICAI handbook; KIP Financial cites 'Clause 1')
schemes.notes: NOT VERIFIED; from secondary sources only (ICAI MSME & Startup Committee 'Madhya Pradesh State MSME Policy' 2026 handbook; KIP Financial consultancy summary). 40% of eligible investment in plant & machinery, building and other listed items made before commercial production. Paid in 4 equal annual instalments. Building cost counted only up to 100% of P&M cost. Applies to units with P&M investment up to Rs 10 crore. Women/SC/ST-owned units (at least 51%) get +2% p.a. for 4 years (+2.5% for SC/ST women). Exporters get +2% p.a. for 4 years if exports are 25-50% of sales, or +3% if above 50%. No absolute cap was found in the sources. Units above Rs 10 crore P&M (medium) instead get 'Investment Promotion Assistance' up to 40%, paid over 7 years under a formula with multipliers (Annexure-II). That formula was not captured.

schemes.name: Quality certification reimbursement (domestic: ISO, BIS, BEE, ISI, FPO, AGMARK)
schemes.clause: MSME Development Policy 2025, section 7.2(i) (per ICAI handbook)
schemes.notes: NOT VERIFIED; ICAI handbook only. 100% of cost, cumulative cap Rs 20 lakh per unit over the policy period. International/export certifications: 50% up to Rs 50 lakh (7.2(ii)). Patents/IPR: 100% up to Rs 10 lakh per patent (7.3).

schemes.name: Sector package interest subsidy (e.g. textiles/pharma) for MSMEs above Rs 5 crore P&M
schemes.clause: MSME Development Policy 2025, section 8.1(iv) (per ICAI handbook)
schemes.notes: NOT VERIFIED; ICAI handbook only, and the handbook's sector attribution is unclear. 5% on term loans for 5 years, max Rs 1 crore per year, for sector-package units with P&M above Rs 5 crore. Food processing units above Rs 5 crore reportedly get a Rs 1/unit power tariff subsidy for 5 years (8.2(ii)(a)) and 100% mandi fee reimbursement for 5 years (8.2). Do not use without the official text.

other_benefits: Unverified (secondary): inland freight for exporters at 50% up to Rs 40 lakh/yr for 5 years; testing lab 50% up to Rs 20 lakh; green industrialization (waste management, pollution control, water conservation) at 50% up to Rs 50 lakh per unit, and CETP for 5+ MSMEs up to Rs 100 lakh; patent 100% up to Rs 10 lakh
unverifiable: The official MSME Development Policy 2025 text could not be obtained. mpmsme.gov.in returned 503 or connection resets. invest.mp.gov.in redirects to a JavaScript single-window app (sws.invest.mp.gov.in) whose bundle links only Energy/Export/Logistics/Health/Start-up policy PDFs. The TeamLease RegTech attachment (blob storage) is gone (ResourceNotFound). All MP figures are therefore verified=false.

The MP Investment Promotion Scheme 2025 (official document, copy on nsws.gov.in) was obtained, but it covers LARGE and mega units under IPP 2025, not MSMEs (its section 1). It was not used for MSME figures.
Validity: per secondary sources, effective 2025-02-24 and in force until amended/replaced. No fixed end date was confirmed.
Electricity duty exemption and SGST reimbursement for MSMEs: not found in any source; MP MSME incentives are capital-subsidy based.
The ICAI handbook text shows signs of paraphrase/auto-generation (e.g. 'sigmoidal curve basic model') and should not be relied on for exact figures.
